It keeps her three run days with rest between them and her dog walks, and it gives a credible path to the November 5K. Volume stays modest. Run and walk segments are unchanged, at 22, 22 and 26 minutes, plus a short bodyweight strength session. This is roughly in line with or slightly above the ~6.8 km she did, which is not a sharp jump. Her calf tightness clears up overnight, so it reads as normal soreness rather than an injury sign. The draft mentions it on the rest days and keeps the effort easy. Each day can be run as written. Minor gaps: the draft never says exactly how she should lengthen the run segments in later weeks. It also doesn't say what to do if the calves stop clearing by the next morning. The '10 weeks' timeline is stated without being tied to her actual race date.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Keep to three run days with a rest day between them, and make the run segments feel easier than they did last week. …
Answers: (1) No, don't run every day next week. Your fitness improves faster than your calves, tendons and joints adapt, and they need rest days to cope with each run. (2) Three runs with a rest day between, plus your dog walks, is the quickest safe route. The gain comes from lengthening the run pieces week by week, and ten weeks is enough time for that.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 22 min, same run and walk lengths as last week, running about two minutes…
Tue: rest, no running, dog walk as usual at a relaxed pace. Your calves get a day to…
Wed: easy, 22 min, same pattern and the same easy effort as Monday. Repeating the same…
Thu: other, 10 min, bodyweight strength: 2 rounds of 10 squats, 10 glute bridges and 10…
Fri: rest, dog walk as usual. Keeps your legs fresh for Saturday's longer run.
Sat: long, 26 min, same pattern at easy effort 4 to 5 out of 10. If your legs feel heavy…
Sun: rest, easy dog walk only. Lets your body absorb the longest run of the week.
